title: A Distributional Framework for Behavioral Characterization and Risk Management of Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.12718v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models are stochastic by nature. Repeated executions under the same experimental conditions may produce different responses. We propose a framework that can be applied across the model lifecycle, from task design to residual behavior and continuous monitoring. The method consists of building an empirical response distribution estimated through Monte Carlo simulation. Semantic interventions are introduced to study how these distributions change. We illustrate the framework with two different tasks, borrower classification and music album recommendation, and quantify the resulting distributional changes. The framework is linked to model risk management and governance by measuring robustness and control effectiveness, and characterizing residual behavior. Since it relies only on observed responses, it can also be applied to black-box models accessed through commercial APIs.

translated_title: 大语言模型行为刻画与风险管理的分布框架
translated_abstract: 大语言模型本质上是随机的，在相同实验条件下重复执行可能产生不同的响应。我们提出了一个可应用于模型全生命周期的框架，从任务设计到残差行为分析和持续监控。该方法通过蒙特卡洛模拟估计来构建经验响应分布，并引入语义干预来研究这些分布如何变化。我们用两个不同的任务，借款人分类和音乐专辑推荐，来演示该框架，并量化由此产生的分布变化。该框架通过测量鲁棒性和控制有效性、刻画残差行为，与模型风险管理和治理相联系。由于它仅依赖于观测到的响应，因此也可应用于通过商业API访问的黑盒模型。
tldr: 该论文提出一个基于蒙特卡洛模拟构建经验响应分布的框架，通过语义干预量化分布变化，将大语言模型的随机行为刻画与模型风险管理、治理以及黑盒模型监控联系起来。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a framework that builds empirical response distributions via Monte Carlo simulation and quantifies changes under semantic interventions, linking stochastic LLM behavioral characterization to model risk management, governance, and black-box model monitoring.
